jobs.prompt: Owner decision (explicit, the owner set these numbers): make the Anthropic API lanes real swarm workers with $500 credit. (1) CAPS: tools/anthropic.mjs DAY_CAP_USD from 20 to 25 (owner-approved; TOTAL_CAP_USD stays 500, per-job cap unchanged); the machine-wide billed day cap behaves in mode 'stop' (a job that would pass the cap is refused before it is sent, nothing queued silently); the cap is the same on every Mac (it lives in code, not a per-machine file); add a test for the new numbers and for stop mode. (2) ROUTING by job type and tier for agent 'auto' (tools/router.mjs, tools/job-types.mjs, docs/job-types.md): order is local endpoint first (only when a healthy 'local' lane exists; the local lane is built in parallel, so code the slot defensively: skipped if the agent is unknown) for diagnose/test/docs/small low-risk fixes; then Haiku API as the main parallel worker for build/fix/test/docs; Sonnet API for hard builds (risk high, size large, or after one Haiku failure) and for normal reviews; Opus API ONLY for security reviews (job type review with sensitive or a new tier/flag securityReview true; the existing opus-needs-tier rule stays); Cursor stays in the mix as today; Codex is skipped (treat lane 'codex' as paused by default via a config flag lanes.codex.paused true that the owner flips back when credits return; implement the flag if missing and ship it set to paused in the default config). Escalate to the next lane only after 2 failures at a lane (keep any existing escalation rule if it already does this). (3) PARALLEL: Haiku and Sonnet API jobs run in parallel up to the machine limit (no per-lane subscription quota applies to API lanes); verify the lane scheduler gives API lanes the machine limit as their concurrency and add a test. (4) PROMPT CACHING: shared repo context already uses cache_control in tools/api-adapters.mjs; verify a wave of jobs with identical context sends the same cached prefix (stable ordering, cache_control on the last shared block, system prompt identical), record cache_read/cache_creation tokens in usage and cost (cached reads priced at the cache-read rate in usageCostUsd) with tests. (5) BATCH: non-urgent review jobs use the Batch API by default when the manifest does not mark them urgent (see docs/batch.md and tools/batch.mjs); make the default explicit in the router/config with a flag batch.reviews default true and an urgent:true job field that bypasses it; tests. Do not touch the board or the usage-API billing (separate work). Keep existing router, lanes, anthropic, batch tests passing (update a test only where a number or order changed by design, with a short comment).
